title: Soy Ginger Steak-On-A-Stick Marinade
servings: About 3½ cups marinade (enough for 3 lb steak, 6 servings)

items: ½ cup packed dark brown sugar
3 tbsp fresh ginger, peeled and minced
3 lb flank, skirt or sirloin steak, about 1 inch thick

steps: Whisk the olive oil, soy sauce, molasses, brown sugar, mirin and dry mustard in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves, about 1 min.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, scallions, red pepper flakes and pineapple juice if using. Season with salt and pepper, going light on the salt since soy sauce is already salty.

Divide the steak between 2 gallon-size zip-top bags and pour the marinade over it. Press out the air, seal and refrigerate 4 to 12 hr, turning once. If you added pineapple juice, keep it to 8 hr or less so the meat doesn't turn mushy.

Take the steak out of the fridge 30 min before cooking. Heat the grill or grill pan over high heat to about 450°F. Lift the steak from the marinade, let the excess drip off and pat it dry. Throw out the used marinade.

Grill the steak 4 to 6 min per side, until well charred. Check with an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part: 130–135°F for medium-rare or 140–145°F for medium. Move it to a cooler spot if the sugars flare up or burn.
Rest the steak on a cutting board 5 to 10 min. Slice thinly against the grain and serve.
tips: Never reuse marinade that touched raw meat. Set aside ½ cup before adding the steak if you want some for drizzling.
The pineapple juice stretches the batch for more meat, but its enzymes soften steak fast, so watch the time.
This also works on chicken thighs or pork tenderloin. Cook chicken to 165°F and pork to 145°F with a 3 min rest.
storage: Unused marinade keeps in a sealed jar in the fridge up to 1 week or frozen up to 3 months. Cooked steak keeps in the fridge 3 to 4 days; reheat gently in a skillet over medium-low heat or eat it cold on salads.
